clusters.description: Diagnose and fix Python interpreter/virtualenv mismatches where pytest, pip, tox, CI, or IDE use different Python environments, causing ImportError or ModuleNotFoundError despite dependencies appearing installed. Workflow: reproduce and read traceback, confirm actual interpreter vs project virtualenv, fix dependencies in the correct project environment, then run targeted and full pytest verification.
clusters.similarity_reason: All six tasks share identical final_steps: '复现并读取 traceback', '确认实际 Python 解释器与 virtualenv', '在项目环境修复依赖', '定向与全量 pytest 验证'. Each involves a different trigger (CLI runner cache, global site-packages, tox, VS Code terminal, pip/pytest mismatch, CI environment) but the root cause and resolution workflow are the same: interpreter/virtualenv mismatch causing test failures.
clusters.reusable_value: High value: this is a recurring class of Python environment misconfiguration that wastes significant debugging time. A reusable diagnostic procedure (check which interpreter each tool uses, align to project .venv, verify with pytest) would save hours per occurrence and prevent repeated trial-and-error fixes.

distillations.reason: The six completed tasks all share the same root cause (Python interpreter/virtualenv mismatch) and the same stable workflow (reproduce and read traceback, confirm actual interpreter vs project virtualenv, fix dependencies in the correct project environment, then run targeted and full pytest verification). This is the same task family as the existing 'debug-python' skill (Python error/test-failure troubleshooting), but the existing skill body only covers generic traceback reading and minimal code fixes. The new tasks add stable, repeated steps specific to interpreter/environment mismatches (checking which interpreter each tool uses, aligning to project .venv, avoiding global pip, verifying with targeted and full pytest). These naturally extend the existing skill rather than forming an independent family.
